texts.firmware.disk.about: %1, the image of %2 of 4D Sports Boxing (Distinctive Software, 1991, DOS), a 720 KB floppy. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. Open4DBoxing reads the game's files from the image as the original read them from the floppy, and never writes to it. Another image of the same floppy, or one of your own, can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.mt32_rom.about: %1 is not one of the game's files. It is %2. You have to supply it when the sound is the MT-32's, because this package includes none of it. Another MT-32 ROM that Munt knows can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.what.disk1: the first floppy, with the four programs (MCGA/VGA, EGA, CGA, Tandy) and the sound drivers
texts.firmware.what.disk2: the second floppy, with the rings, the boxers' heads and the rest of the pictures and sounds
texts.firmware.what.mt32_control: the control ROM of the Roland MT-32, version 1.07, dumped from a unit of the first generation
texts.firmware.what.mt32_pcm: the PCM ROM of the Roland MT-32, which is the same in every MT-32
texts.property.build: The program that runs, as the Video setting chose it
texts.property.down: Set while the %1 boxer is down
texts.property.ended: The player left the game (its EXIT)
texts.property.endurance: The %1 boxer's endurance, the O bar against his maximum: 10 a punch thrown, and drained by lost health
texts.property.frame: Video frames shown: 70.086 a second on the VGA, 59.92 on the EGA, the CGA and the Tandy
texts.property.health: The %1 boxer's health, the D bar: 16384 fresh; a landed punch takes from it, below 1 floors him
texts.property.manual_question: The name the manual's question asks for, chosen when it is asked (9, the champion's face, wants the ow of Stan Chow: the original's own slip)
texts.property.punches: In the round, as the round's statistics count them
texts.property.random_state: The C library's rand() state (x = x * 0x343FD + 0x269EC3), never seeded: the game's randomness is how many times it ran
texts.property.stamina: The %1 boxer's stamina, the P bar: 16384 fresh; a punch thrown and a block cost it
texts.setting.clock_start.about: The PC's date and time when the game starts, written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (the default is the date of the game's programs on its floppies). The clock then advances with the game, and the BIOS's tick count starts from the time of day. A movie records the start time it ran with.
texts.setting.cosmetic_camera.about: The ring's cameras (F1-F10) shown without the game seeing their keys. In the original a camera key changes the fight: a view takes its own time to draw, and the fight reads a value its drawing leaves behind, so a movie made without the cameras desyncs with them. With this on, the game always runs with its own camera, and a second copy of it, given the game's fight at every frame and the camera keys alone, draws the picture: the camera work can be added to a finished movie. Changes the picture only (the MCGA program; the others ignore it).
texts.setting.cpu_speed.about: The PC's speed, as DOSBox's cycles: the instructions it runs a millisecond (the default, 22,000, is the 486 of the DOSBox-X machine Open4DBoxing was checked against). The game's frames take its time, and in a fight the boxers' moves go by the game's timer: at 220,000 every frame fits in one of the timer's 10 ms ticks, and the fight goes the same whatever the frames draw. A movie records the speed it ran with.
texts.setting.sound.about: The sound driver the game loads, as its setup chose it: the Roland MT-32 (the default), the Sound Blaster (its FM music with the digitised announcer and crowd), the AdLib, the PC speaker or the Tandy's sound chip. The MT-32 needs the two ROMs of an MT-32 (version 1.07, the first generation), which the project supplies as firmware.
texts.setting.video.about: Which of the game's four programs runs, one for each video card: the MCGA/VGA (256 colours, the default), the EGA (16 colours), the CGA (4 colours) or the Tandy 1000 (16 colours). The MCGA's program runs at the VGA's 70 frames a second, the others at 60. The game's properties (the boxers' health, stamina and endurance) are known for the MCGA's program only.
